Name: neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mpp
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mpp during legal execution can corrupt, suppress, or mis-time the protected primary asset.
Justification: MPP supplies the effective LSU privilege under MPRV, so a fault can elevate or corrupt ctrl_o.lsu_priv.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on neorv32_cpu_control.csr.mstatus_mprv during legal execution can corrupt, suppress, or mis-time the protected primary asset.
Justification: MPRV selects whether data accesses use MPP, making a fault capable of switching the privilege source seen by the LSU.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.csr.prv_level
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on neorv32_cpu_control.csr.prv_level during legal execution can corrupt, suppress, or mis-time the protected primary asset.
Justification: The architectural privilege register directly feeds effective LSU privilege, so its corruption can change access authority.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl.csr_we
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on neorv32_cpu_control.ctrl.csr_we during legal execution can corrupt, suppress, or mis-time the protected primary asset.
Justification: A spurious or suppressed CSR write can corrupt the privilege state subsequently used to form ctrl_o.lsu_priv.

Name: neorv32_cpu_control.env_exit
Attack Scenarios: A transient fault on neorv32_cpu_control.env_exit during legal execution can corrupt, suppress, or mis-time the protected primary asset.
Justification: This environment-return control triggers privilege restoration; a fault can apply the wrong privilege transition to LSU accesses.
